newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Polar, RFC surge, hit ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Polar, RFC surge, hit ceiling.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Friday froze any further rise in the share prices of Polar Mines and Development Corp and investment firm RFC Inc.

The bourse's surveillance department said the two stocks reached the 50 percent price rise ceiling. Under the rules, the exchange can freeze the share price of an issue when the ceiling is reached in a single trading session.
The bourse issued the freeze order after Polar climbed to 23 centavos from 15.50 centavos while RFC reached 25.50 pesos from 17 pesos in early trade.
The PSE said it decided to halt trading in RFC shares until the company gave reasons for the surge.

Answering the bourse's query on the stock's steep climb earlier this week, RFC said it is not aware of any material disclosure except possibly for its purchase of a 30 percent stake in a small private development bank.

Polar Mines disclosed on Friday that its board has approved an increase in authorised capital stock to 13 billion pesos from 100 million pesos and raised its par value from one centavo to one peso per share.
Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities, said the surge in Polar prices may be due to its proposed increase in capital and par value.
"If you have that increase in capital, then investors would believe the company has big plans," said Fitz Aclan, research head at Dharmala Securities.
Some one billion shares of Polar and 30,000 RFC shares were being traded when their prices were frozen, the PSE said.
